title: What Are Archaea?
hook: Archaea are the third domain of life — single-celled microbes that look like bacteria but are genetically a world apart, and many thrive in extreme places.
key_points: Archaea make up one of the three domains of life, alongside Bacteria and Eukarya.
They are single-celled microbes with no nucleus, like bacteria.
Genetically and chemically, they differ sharply from bacteria.
Many are extremophiles, living in boiling springs, salt lakes, and deep vents.
They are not just oddities — archaea live in soil, oceans, and even your gut.
content_html: Archaea are single-celled microbes that, for a long time, were mistaken for unusual bacteria. They look similar under a microscope — tiny, no nucleus — but their genes and cell chemistry are so different that biologists place them in their own domain. That makes three great branches of life: Bacteria, Archaea, and Eukarya (everything with nucleated cells, including us).
extra_html: Archaea earned their separate domain in the late 1970s, when comparisons of their genetic material revealed how deeply they diverge from ordinary bacteria. Many are famous extremophiles, thriving where almost nothing else can: scalding hot springs, briny lakes, and high-pressure deep-sea vents. But they aren't only exotic — archaea are everywhere, including ordinary soil, the open ocean, and the human gut, where some help with digestion. Encyclopaedia Britannica's overview of archaea describes how these ancient microbes came to be recognized as the third domain of life.

related.title: The Three Domains of Life
related.hook: At the very top, all life splits into just three branches — Bacteria, Archaea, and Eukarya — and your cells belong to the same one as mushrooms and oak trees.

related.title: What Are Bacteria?
related.hook: Single-celled and everywhere — in soil, oceans, and your gut — bacteria run much of the planet's chemistry, and most of them never make you sick.

related.title: Two Kinds of Cells
related.hook: All cells fall into two camps: simple prokaryotes with no nucleus, and complex eukaryotes that pack their DNA into a sealed control room.

flashcards.prompt: Which three domains make up all of life, and where do archaea fit?
flashcards.back_html: Life is split into Bacteria, Archaea, and Eukarya. Archaea are the third domain — single-celled microbes distinct from both bacteria and eukaryotes.

flashcards.prompt: Why aren't archaea simply classified as a kind of bacteria?

choices.text: Their genetics and cell chemistry differ sharply from bacteria
They are much larger than any bacterium
They have a true nucleus like animal cells

flashcards.explanation_html: Archaea look bacteria-like under a microscope, but their genes and cell chemistry set them apart enough to form their own domain.

choices.text: One that thrives in extreme conditions like boiling or super-salty water
An archaeon that can only live inside human cells
A microbe that has gone extinct

flashcards.explanation_html: Many archaea are extremophiles — they flourish in environments like hot springs, salt lakes, and deep-sea vents that would kill most other life.
